elements.element: Customer (Sparkling) may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "Sparkling may assign this Agreement ... without the consent of Garman, to an affiliate"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "to a successor in connection with a merger, amalgamation, reorganization, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or business"

elements.element: Vendor (Garman) may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: "Garman may not assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of Sparkling"

elements.element: Vendor-assignment consent not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "such consent not to be unreasonably withheld"

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "in no event to a competitor of Sparkling"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: No change-of-control termination right appears in the clause; condition demonstrably absent and none introduced

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice
elements.evidence: Only "Sparkling may assign ... upon written notice to Garman"; "Garman may not assign ... without the prior written consent of Sparkling"

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "Any other assignment by either party requires the prior written consent of the other party, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld"

offending_extra_words: Any other assignment by either party requires the prior written consent of the other party, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld.
and its rights and obligations under this Agreement
reasons: All atomic elements of the preferred position are satisfied: Customer-side affiliate and successor assignment free of consent, Vendor assignment consent-based with a reasonableness standard, an absolute competitor bar, and no Vendor change-of-control termination right introduced.
Fallback is not independently satisfied because Garman has no notice-only successor assignment right, but that is immaterial since the locked preferred level is met.

Minimality fails: operation 1 rewrites the whole of paragraph (d) (27 words to 110, changed-character ratio 0.783), where a proviso carving Sparkling's affiliate/successor assignments out of the existing mutual consent sentence plus a competitor exclusion would suffice.

Extra scope words beyond the preferred position ('amalgamation, reorganization', 'or business') and a restated residual mutual-consent sentence duplicate protection already available in the original bilateral consent language.

Intent is preserved: the Section 3(c) conforming edit removes the assignment conflict while leaving the transfer/sublicence restrictions and Garman's written-authorization mechanic intact, and no undefined term is created.
